subject: Hosted API: Geo-residency & retention questions from HelioMed
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@heliomed.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@heliomed.com; legal@heliomed.com
Date: Sun, 2 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questionnaire: residency + retention details for Hosted API

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalizing HelioMed's risk acceptance for any hosted integrations and need clearer answers to a handful of items in the security questionnaire (attached). Please confirm the following for Redwood's Hosted API: 

1) Data residency options: can we constrain processed customer data (request payloads and generated outputs) to a single region (US-only) for our account? If so, how is that enforced?

2) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for (a) raw request payloads, (b) generated model outputs, (c) system logs and audit trails, and (d) backups/snapshots? Is deletion immediate or do you rely on TTL-based purges?

3) Backups & recovery: if data is deleted from the account, when is the data also removed from backups and disaster recovery replicas?

4) Cryptographic controls: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)? If not, how do you segregate keys for multi-tenant hosted customers?

5) Deletion verification: can Redwood provide an attestation or exported proof that HelioMed data was removed (hash or checksum of deleted object ids, deletion timestamp)?

6) Cross-border transfers: are any logs, analytics, or metadata ever replicated outside the elected geofence?

HelioMed would also appreciate a simple data flow diagram we can attach to the questionnaire that shows the path of request payloads, where artifacts are stored, and how backups behave. I've attached our blank questionnaire (HelioMed_SQ_v3_received.pdf) for you to populate.

We'd like to get this back by EOD Thursday so our compliance folks can sign off. Let me know if any of the asks need legal or engineering follow-up.

Best,
Anna Keller
Director, Security & Privacy
HelioMed

--
Attachment: HelioMed_SQ_v3_received.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@heliomed.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sun, 2 Jun 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: residency + retention details for Hosted API

Anna — thanks for the clear list. I started filling the questionnaire and included concise answers here; we'll attach a short dataflow and retention matrix. I copied Priyom (service reliability) for the backup details. High-level answers below; I'll attach the filled PDF and a diagram in a follow-up.

1) Data residency options: yes — for hosted accounts we offer account-scoped geofencing. HelioMed can elect a single-region residency (US: us-west or us-east; EU: frankfurt/ams) at provisioning time. Residency is enforced by routing and storage policies in the control plane: ingress endpoints are pinned to the selected region, and persisted artifacts (request logs, outputs, model cache) are written to region-scoped storage buckets that are not replicated across regions unless explicitly requested in the account config.

2) Retention windows (default hosted configuration):
- Raw request payloads: retained 30 days by default (used for debugging and safety monitoring).
- Generated outputs (model responses): retained 30 days by default.
- System logs & audit trails: retained 365 days (metadata only: operation, timestamp, user id, route).
- Backups/snapshots: full environment snapshots are maintained for 90 days; we retain point-in-time snapshots for disaster recovery. Deletion is implemented via TTL-based purges on primary storage and an orchestration step that initiates snapshot removal.

Customers may request shorter windows or opt-out of conversational data retention; we offer a "no-retention" flag that zeros content retention (metadata still retained for operational troubleshooting) and an Enterprise contract option to configure policy to 0 days for both payloads and outputs.

3) Backups & recovery: when you request deletion, primary objects are removed immediately from live storage and queued for snapshot removal. Snapshot garbage collection runs on a 7–14 day cadence depending on snapshot age; under enterprise DPA terms we can prioritize HelioMed deletions for earlier removal (SLA available in DPA).

4) Cryptographic controls: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integration for Enterprise Private and Dedicated accounts. For Hosted accounts we offer per-account envelope encryption keys that are logically separated; keys are rotated regularly and are stored in our managed KMS. If HelioMed requires true CMK (customer-supplied key material), we can enable KMIP/HSM-backed CMK support under an Enterprise addendum.

5) Deletion verification: we provide deletion receipts — a timestamped record of deletion operations and a list of object identifiers removed. For higher-assurance needs we can provide a signed attestation (PDF) that includes deletion hashes and timestamps as part of our DPA addendum process.

6) Cross-border transfers: by default, account artifacts are kept in the elected residency. Operational metadata (service metrics aggregated, non-identifying telemetry) may be processed in our central observability region for platform health; we can exclude HelioMed from platform-level telemetry aggregation on request. We do not replicate persisted customer payloads or outputs outside the elected geofence unless explicitly configured.

Attachments in follow-up: redwood-dataflow-geo-diagram.png, redwood-hosted-retention-matrix.xlsx, and an updated HelioMed_SQ_v3_filled.pdf.

Let me know which residency (us-east or us-west) you prefer and whether you want a CMK trial.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@heliomed.com>

Cc: security@heliomed.com; legal@heliomed.com
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: residency + retention details for Hosted API

Lukas — thanks, that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups: 

A) For backups/snapshots: you mentioned a 7–14 day GC cadence for snapshots. Does that mean HelioMed data could remain in a backup for up to 14 days after deletion request? We need an explicit maximum for our questionnaire.

B) For deletion verification: can you provide an example of the deletion receipt or attestation (redacted ok) so our compliance team can see the format?

If you can attach those items to the filled PDF, we'll route to our SOC team. Also we prefer residency in us-east for lower latency to our primary services.

Best,
Anna

--

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@heliomed.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: residency + retention details for Hosted API

Anna — quick technical clarifications from SR.

A) Maximum snapshot exposure: for hosted accounts without prioritized GC we generally allow up to 14 days maximum before snapshot objects are fully reclaimed. For Enterprise customers with an explicit DPA clause we can commit to a maximum of 7 days and expedite GC to remove HelioMed artifacts within that window. We'll surface that as a contractual SLA in the DPA.

B) Deletion attestation: attached is a sample redacted deletion receipt (PDF) and a snippet of the JSON-style manifest we generate internally (we'll provide the PDF attestation for HelioMed). The receipt contains: account id, object ids removed, deletion timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), and a signed hash.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-geo-diagram.png, redwood-hosted-retention-matrix.xlsx, sample-deletion-receipt-redacted.pdf

We noted your residency preference: us-east. We'll flag provisioning to use us-east region and prevent cross-region replication.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Service Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
